_about: Language-agnostic spec for a deterministic cost-tier router. THIS FILE is the reusable asset: any app (Go/Rust/TS/Python/bash) loads it and implements the matcher — lowercase the task, select a tier per `strategy`, then apply length_rules → bias → escalation → clamps. See README.md. route.sh is the reference implementation; bench.sh scores any implementation against evalset.tsv.
_strategy_note: first-match (walk rules in order, first match wins) | max-hits (tier with most matching rules wins) | weighted (sum of rule.weight per tier). Default first-match keeps parity with compass-route.sh.
_bias_note: cheap | balanced | quality. On a LOW-confidence pick only: cheap downgrades one tier, quality upgrades one — never past clamps. balanced = no change.

haiku.use: mechanical / low-reasoning: typos, renames, formatting, comments, version bumps, one-liners

sonnet.use: default: features, fixes, tests, refactors, docs

opus.use: high-stakes reasoning: architecture, security/auth/crypto, concurrency, migrations, multi-tenancy, protocol/threat design

_cost_note: cost is a RELATIVE weight (~output $/Mtok ratio: haiku 1 : sonnet 4 : opus 20). Override per app via `profiles`.
_profiles_note: select with --profile NAME; a profile overrides per-tier cost/model. Use it so bench.sh savings reflect YOUR prices and so each app (lantern/kage) maps tiers to its own models.
_clamps_note: hard bounds applied LAST. floor = never route below; ceiling = never above (cost cap). allow = explicit allowlist (overrides floor/ceiling when non-empty). Override per run: --floor/--ceiling/--allow.
_escalation_note: if the pick's confidence < threshold (0 = off): when `fallback` is set it is run (the task is piped on stdin; it prints a tier) and that tier is used — the cascade: heuristic for the confident majority, a smarter call (LLM/classifier) for the ambiguous middle. With no fallback, the tier is bumped one step. Override: --escalate-below N, --fallback CMD.
_length_note: raise the floor for long tasks: a task with >= min_words is forced to at least `at_least` (a 60-word 'comment …' task isn't really trivial). Applied before bias/escalation.
_rules_note: ordered. Each: tier, pattern (ERE, matched case-insensitively), reason, optional `weight` (max-hits/weighted strategies), optional `unless` (ERE that VETOES this rule when it also matches — e.g. opus 'unless' a trivial qualifier).
_domains_note: optional SECOND axis (orthogonal to tier): --domain also emits a specialist (ui/api/infra/docs/core) via first-match, for apps that dispatch to domain agents. 'core' is the catch-all.
